text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Fatos Nano's decision to reduce the ministerial workforce by 15 percent should be applied carefully in separate institutions, newspaper editorial says.

- The Republican Guard demands 25 people from the former presidential staff, including Genc Pollo, secretary general of the Democratic Party, hand in Kalashnikovs handed out during the state of emergency.
- A study from the IMF, World Bank and EU, sent to the Albanian government for approval, says the Balkan country needs three years until it can be on the road of stable economic development.
- Together with the operation to crush gangster bands in the southern port town of Vlore, special police forces have now started collecting in weapons.
- Arben Rakipi, new chief prosecutor general, says the justice system should be rid of corrupt staff and those with no professional capabilities.
- Adem Copani, armed forces chief of staff, says bad treatment and low salaries were to blame for the poor state of the army.
- FIFA decided that Albania's home World Cup Group Nine qualifier versus Northern Ireland on September 10 will be played in Zurich.
- Police say Zan Caushi, head of a gang in Vlore, has left for Italy. This has been denied by the Italian foreign ministry.
- Four were killed and 12 injured in an armed clash between police and an unidentified group in the town of Elbasan.
- Elmaz Sherifi, the labour minister, believes unemployment might be 40 percent and not the official figure of 11.5 percent.
- Referring to a government source, the newspaper says the value-added tax will soon be increased from 12.5 percent to 18 percent.
- Opposition Democratic Party MPs walked out of a parliamentary session claiming parliament is not legitimate.
